techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_observability/libs/useGlobalAlertEvaluator.ts:53 a persona-scoped rule is evaluated against project-wide data, then shares the rule.id cooldown with the scoped evaluator at src-tauri/src/commands/execution/alert_evaluator.rs:170 - scope is in the key but not in the detection, so the wrong-scope fire consumes the scoped rule's cooldown

src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:152 the fired message is a bare 'metric is value (threshold)' with no contributor breakdown - the homework alert; this obligation does not lapse for a local reader

src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:499 delivery is an in-app toast to the single local operator - no broadcast audience, so the payload-bounding rule lapses per the golden path's audience precondition
src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:499 alerts never leave the process as webhooks in this context; no operator-supplied destination to sign or vet

pairs.registryProposal: The subject's techniques assume one evaluator; a recurring field shape here is TWO evaluators (client + server) sharing one cooldown key with different scope semantics. scoped-dedup-keys could name it: when more than one evaluator writes the same dedup key, each must evaluate the identical scope, or the less-scoped one silently suppresses the authoritative one.
